name: SMT-LIB
summary: The common input and command language of satisfiability-modulo-theories (SMT) solvers: an S-expression syntax for many-sorted first-order formulas over standardised background theories (integers, reals, bit-vectors, arrays, floating point, strings, datatypes) plus a script language (declare-fun, assert, check-sat, get-model, push/pop) with an operational semantics for interacting with solvers.

level_notes.1: Defined by the SMT-LIB Standard reference document (Barrett, Fontaine, Tinelli; v2.7 of 2025, v2.6 still the most widely implemented), plus the separate machine-readable theory and logic declarations on smt-lib.org. Section links use #page=N into the PDF (PDF page = printed page + 1). Solver manuals (cvc5, Z3) document non-standard theories (sequences, sets, bags, finite fields).
level_notes.0: No single reference implementation: Z3, cvc5, Yices 2, Bitwuzla, MathSAT and OpenSMT each implement their own SMT-LIB parser; Dolmen is a standalone parser/typechecker that tracks the standard closely.
level_notes.3: No PLDB entry was found for SMT-LIB.
